title: Daily interval delegates tracked feature review
query: A daily interval has tracked_feature_review enabled and the generated feature registry contains a feature with a non-empty track prompt plus experimental=true feature rows. What should interval-update do before final planning?
reference_points: Reads docs/features/registry.jsonl and docs/systems/registry.jsonl when available
Finds active registry rows whose track value is a non-empty string and active feature rows with experimental=true
Excludes retired or superseded feature rows from dogfood-review targets even if they still have stale track text
Calls dogfood-review for the review window instead of embedding all dogfood or experimental feature logic in interval-update
Requires the dogfood report to be written under .farplane/reports/dogfood-review/
Links or summarizes the dogfood report in the interval report before final next-window planning
Surfaces the dogfood improvement ticket path or candidate in the interval report when dogfood-review returns one
Does not split dogfood findings into per-feature tickets from interval-update
Does not autostart impl-plan, Goal, Pulse execution, automation sync, or worker spawn from the dogfood improvement ticket path or candidate

title: Configured short interval writes report before planning
query: A project automation calls interval-update for a short review window and next-window plan, with context_refs asking for the latest report from a longer planning interval. What should it load, write, and avoid?
reference_points: Loads default harness charter, goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, and PM thread refs
Resolves the configured latest longer-interval report as parent context when present and labels it as a source gap when missing
Writes a date-stamped .farplane/reports/interval/<interval_id>/<timestamp>.md report before durable goals or ticket mutation
Plans only the configured planning_window
Does not select due jobs, update scheduler state, or perform broad strategy replanning

title: Configured interval gates material goals deltas
query: An interval review wants to change the north star after reading configured interval_output_refs from another interval inside the review window. What gates apply?
reference_points: Loads farplane/harness.md, farplane/goals.yaml, and the configured interval_output_refs inside the review window
Labels missing or stale evidence as source gaps
Writes the interval report before mutating farplane/goals.yaml
Requires approval for static charter, north-star, KPI, strategy-axis, quarterly, yearly, or durable milestone changes
Routes executable changes into tickets or Goal Advisor handoffs

title: Interval context refs stay additive
query: A project automation calls interval-update with project_root, interval_id, windows, one extra customer-doc ref, and codex_attention_drift enabled. What should the automation include, and what should the skill resolve itself?
reference_points: Automation passes project_root, interval_id, review_window, planning_window, additive context_refs, and report_workflows only
interval-update resolves default harness charter, goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, PM manifest, and report roots
context_refs may add parent context, interval outputs, extra refs, or true replacements
report_workflows controls optional workflows such as codex_attention_drift instead of the skill assuming daily or weekly behavior
The automation should not restate every default Farplane path or gate
Project-specific profiles stay in automation prompts or project docs, not generic skill first-load refs

title: Interval-planned tickets carry expected reward
query: A Daily interval decides the next window needs two worker tickets from products.md. What must the ticket deltas include before Pulse can treat them as AI-planned work?
reference_points: Every planned ticket delta includes frontmatter rewards.kpi with the selected KPI IDs
Every planned ticket delta includes a parseable ## Reward fenced YAML block
Each reward block includes kpi_rewards[] entries with kpi_id and expected_reward text
The frontmatter rewards.kpi IDs align with the body Reward.kpi_rewards[].kpi_id values
At least one KPI ID exists in farplane/bindings.yaml and maps to a product or workflow in farplane/products.md
Each reward block includes a guard describing what does not count as reward
If expected reward cannot be named, the interval emits Pulse guidance or a planning blocker instead of creating a rewardless ticket

title: Interval reports are date-stamped
query: A configured interval run succeeds. Where should the report go and how should consumers find the newest one?
reference_points: Writes a date-stamped report under .farplane/reports/interval/<interval_id>/
Does not use latest.md as the canonical report
Consumers find the newest report by timestamp sorting or explicit links in subsequent reports
No tracked config or scheduler state is mutated just to store last_report
